strengths: Provides a rigorous and novel connection between the statistical physics view of 'symmetry breaking class speciation' and information-theoretic class-conditional entropy.
Discovers a notable difference in the phase-transition behavior between VP and VE/EDM SDEs under high-dimensional limits, showing that only VP exhibits a sharp localized transition in rescaled time.
Introduces 'partitioned class-conditional entropy' to resolve hierarchical semantic choices, allowing the analysis of fine-grained attribute emergence at different scales.
Offers a practical, online posterior-tracking algorithm to estimate these entropic curves directly from pre-trained large-scale models without requiring the training dataset.

Provides clear and insightful explanations of why classifier-free guidance is most effective in intermediate noise windows, corroborating prior empirical studies with quantitative information-theoretic evidence.
weaknesses: The online posterior-tracking estimator relies heavily on the calibration and accuracy of the score networks; systematic model errors can distort the estimated entropy profiles.
In the ImageNet-512 experiments, approximating the class complement (Z != i) with the unconditional model is a practical shortcut but introduces unquantified approximation bias.
The text-to-image evaluation on Stable Diffusion 1.5 is somewhat limited and sensitive to prompt selection due to prompt-adherence issues, as acknowledged by the authors.

While the entropic signature serves as a valuable diagnostic tool, the paper does not develop an automated, sample-adaptive guidance or scheduling algorithm based on these measurements, which would significantly enhance its practical utility.

strengths: Bridges statistical physics theories of class speciation with an operational, information-theoretic diagnostic (class-conditional entropy) that can be computed in trained diffusion models.
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis under high-dimensional Gaussian mixture assumptions, identifying why the speciation transition is sharp in VP diffusion but broadens in VE/EDM diffusion.
Introduces a novel partitioned entropy approach to isolate and resolve semantic decisions at different levels of abstraction (e.g., global layout vs. fine-grained objects).
Empirically validates the theory on complex, large-scale models (EDM2-XS and Stable Diffusion 1.5) and uses the framework to explain the impact of different guidance schedules.
weaknesses: The estimation of the partitioned class-conditional entropy relies on a posterior-tracking algorithm which is computationally intensive and requires multiple model evaluations over many Monte Carlo trajectories.

The practical implementation approximates the class complement $Z \neq i$ using the unconditional model. While mathematically convenient, this approximation can introduce biases, particularly when the class distribution is highly imbalanced or non-uniform.

The empirical evaluation on Stable Diffusion 1.5 is limited by the model's poor prompt adherence (as discussed in Section 6 and Appendix C.2), and testing on more modern, well-aligned architectures would reinforce the utility of the method.
While the difference between VP and VE/EDM speciation scaling is theoretically analyzed, its practical implications on sampling schedules or optimal guidance strategies are not fully resolved.

strengths: Elegant theoretical foundation linking information-theoretic class-conditional entropy (and entropy production) to the statistical physics view of spontaneous symmetry breaking and class speciation in diffusion models.

Provides a practical, online posterior-tracking algorithm that allows researchers to estimate these entropic signatures directly in pre-trained, state-of-the-art models (such as EDM2 and Stable Diffusion) without requiring closed-form posteriors.

The introduction of partitioned class-conditional entropy is highly clever, as it allows isolating specific semantic decisions and branching points at varying levels of abstraction and different spatial/spectral frequencies (e.g., global color vs. local object features).

Offers valuable quantitative insights into how classifier-free guidance redistributes information over time, providing a principled explanation for the empirical success of time-localized guidance schedules.
Very high-quality writing and visualization, particularly in Figures 1, 3, and 4, which clearly illustrate the concept of entropy production peaks and their relationship to generated features.
weaknesses: The accuracy of the online posterior-tracking estimator depends heavily on the calibration and prediction accuracy of the conditional and unconditional denoisers across all noise levels, which can lead to biased profiles if the model is uncalibrated.

To estimate the entropy on ImageNet, the unconditional model is used as a proxy for the complement distribution ($Z \neq i$). This approximation can introduce systematic biases if the unconditional distribution significantly deviates from the true complement.

For text-to-image models (e.g., Stable Diffusion 1.5), the method is highly sensitive to prompt adherence and semantic bleeding, where prompt modifications might shift the overall image layout instead of isolating a single attribute (as shown in the failure cases in Appendix C.2).

While the paper identifies that VE/EDM-style forward SDEs do not exhibit the same sharp transition localized around a dimension-independent rescaled time as VP-SDEs do, the practical and operational implications of this difference for VE models remain somewhat under-explored.

strengths: Strong theoretical foundation that elegantly connects information-theoretic entropy production with the statistical physics perspective of symmetry-breaking and class speciation in high-dimensional diffusion processes.

The introduction of 'partitioned' class-conditional entropy is a clever and useful extension, enabling the analysis of hierarchical and fine-grained semantic decisions (e.g., specific attributes) instead of being limited to coarse, global class variables.

Thorough mathematical derivations in the appendix, providing exact closed-form expressions for Gaussian mixtures and formalizing the scaling behavior under both Variance-Preserving (VP) and Variance-Exploding (VE) frameworks.

Compelling empirical validation across diverse and large-scale architectures (EDM2-XS on ImageNet and Stable Diffusion 1.5/XL), supported by intuitive visualizations of how semantic structure emerges alongside entropy production peaks.
Insightful analysis of the impact of Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG), showing quantitatively how guidance redistributes and accelerates information transfer during the reverse process.
weaknesses: The work relies heavily on very recent contemporary works: the theoretical framework is a direct extension of the speciation theory in Achilli et al. (2026), while the practical estimation pipeline is adopted directly from the posterior update algorithm of Koulischer et al. (2025a). This reduces the standalone methodological novelty of the paper.

The computational cost of the proposed diagnostic is extremely high. According to the 'Used resources' section, estimating a single partitioned class-conditional entropy profile takes about 4.0 hours on an enterprise NVIDIA H200 GPU for SDXL 1.0. This severely limits its utility as a practical, lightweight diagnostic tool for model development.

There is a lack of novel actionable algorithms. While the paper claims to provide a 'principled basis for time-localized control,' it does not introduce any new guidance schedulers or sampling techniques based on the entropic signature. It primarily acts as a post-hoc explanatory diagnostic for existing empirical practices (like interval guidance).

To make the estimation tractable in realistic settings, several significant approximations are introduced (such as setting partition priors to 0.5 and substituting the true complement model with the unconditional model). While these are analyzed in the appendix, they introduce a gap between the elegant theoretical formulations in Section 4 and the quantities actually plotted in the experiments.

The estimator's sensitivity to model calibration and prompt adherence (as acknowledged in Section 6 and demonstrated in Figure 13) means that in practice, the diagnostic can easily be corrupted by sub-optimal model behavior rather than reflecting the true semantic transitions of the data distribution.

strengths: Elegant theoretical framework: The paper successfully bridges the statistical physics perspective of symmetry-breaking class speciation and information theory by using class-conditional entropy and its derivative (entropy production) as an operational diagnostic.

Rigorous scaling analysis: The theoretical derivation of the speciation transitions for both VP SDEs (which sharpen into a dimension-independent O(1) window) and VE-EDM SDEs (which broaden as O(√d) on the physical time axis) is highly elegant and provides a novel contribution to our understanding of different diffusion formulations.

Operational applicability: By introducing the partitioned class-conditional entropy with balanced priors, the authors turn a high-dimensional theoretical concept into a practical tool that can be estimated on actual, pre-trained diffusion models.

Insightful empirical findings: The experiments on EDM2-XS (ImageNet) and Stable Diffusion 1.5/SDXL cleanly demonstrate the hierarchical (coarse-to-fine) emergence of semantic features. The analysis of how classifier-free guidance redistributes and distorts this entropy profile over time provides valuable mechanistic insights into why guidance is effective.

High-quality writing and presentation: The paper is exceptionally well-written, with highly intuitive figures (especially Figures 1, 3, and 4) and well-structured appendices that contain complete mathematical proofs.
weaknesses: Reliance on prior estimator and calibration: The proposed operational diagnostic relies heavily on the recursive posterior update scheme from Koulischer et al. (2025a). As the authors note, systematic prediction errors or uncalibrated score networks can bias the posterior updates, meaning the diagnostic is only as good as the underlying model's calibration.

Computational overhead: Computing the partitioned class-conditional entropy requires generating hundreds of samples and running backward posterior updates over many denoising steps. While feasible as an offline diagnostic, this computational cost (e.g., 4 hours for SDXL on an H200) prevents it from being used as an online, real-time controller.

Sensitivity to prompt design in T2I settings: In the text-conditioned experiments, the binary partitions are constructed via manual prompt modifications. If the base and variant prompts have poor adherence or induce unintended distribution shifts, the measured entropy profile may reflect these confounding factors rather than the targeted semantic attribute.

strengths: Strong theoretical grounding that bridges information theory (entropy production) with the statistical physics perspective of class speciation and symmetry breaking in diffusion models.

Provides a rigorous and clean analytical comparison of the speciation dynamics between VP (Variance-Preserving) and VE-EDM (Variance-Exploding) schedules, showing why VP transitions sharpen under dimension scaling while VE-EDM transitions broaden on the physical time axis.

Introduces a highly practical, estimator-based framework (using local posterior updates) that enables the tracking of partitioned class-conditional entropy in realistic, large-scale trained models (EDM2-XS on ImageNet and Stable Diffusion/SDXL on LAION).

Provides valuable empirical insights into the mechanism of Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG), quantitatively showing how guidance redistributes and accelerates entropy reduction/speciation along the trajectory.
weaknesses: The iterative posterior estimation algorithm (Algorithm 1) requires multiple Monte Carlo evaluations over many steps, making it computationally expensive to run on large text-to-image models (e.g., 4 hours for SDXL on a H200 GPU).

The approach is highly sensitive to model quality, calibration, and prompt adherence (as seen in the failure cases in SD 1.5), meaning the diagnostic may capture generation artifacts rather than true semantic speciation when applied to less aligned models.

While the paper provides a diagnostic framework, it does not translate these insights into a novel, actionable control algorithm (such as an adaptive sampling scheduler or optimized guidance scheduler) that directly utilizes the entropic signature online.
